title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 9: intention vs execution — glory destined before foresight of faith
pass_a_gloss: Solution. It is one thing to consider glory destined to the elect before the foundations of the world were laid according to God's intention, another to consider the same conferred on them in time through the execution of the same decree. In God's intention itself glory was predestined, and so great a glory to Stephen, before foresight of his patience and faith: Nay, in the decree of predestination God had prepared for him so great a faith and patience, because he had elected him to so great a glory.
pass_b_english: Sol. One thing is glory destined to the elect before the world's foundations, according to God's intention; another is that same glory conferred on them in time by executing the decree. In God's intention itself glory — and so great a glory — was predestined to Stephen before foresight of his patience and faith. Indeed, in the decree of predestination God had prepared him that faith and patience because he had elected him to that glory.
source_text: Sol. Aliud est considerare gloriam ante jacta mundi fundamenta electis destinatam secundum Dei intentionem, aliud considerare eandem ipsis in tempore collatam per ejusdem decreti exsecutionem. In ipsa Dei intentione praedestinata fuit gloria, et tanta gloria Stephano, ante praescientiam patientiae et fidei ejus: Imo in praedestinationis decreto tantam fidem et patientiam Deus illi praeparaverat, quia ad tantam gloriam illum elegerat.
